summary: Authentication boundaries are enforced through a multi-layer architecture: API middleware validates backend sessions, frontend proxy.ts handles session validation with explicit fail-closed behavior (auth errors redirect to login, never return NextResponse.next()), and Vercel binds the backend URL as CAREGIST_BACKEND_URL. The middleware auth test (frontend/lib/middleware-auth.test.ts) verifies fail-closed behavior. The live site at https://www.caregist.co.uk requires login for Dashboard access. Production deployment has separate frontend (Next.js) and backend (FastAPI) services with distinct auth boundaries.
assertions: API middleware validates sessions; frontend proxy.ts fails closed — errors redirect to login, never pass through
middleware-auth.test.ts verifies: catch block returns redirectToLogin(), does NOT return NextResponse.next()
Live site has /login and /signup routes; Dashboard/Log Out visible only post-authentication
Frontend and backend are separate Vercel services with distinct auth boundaries
Production README: 'Commercial and unapproved mutation paths must remain fail-closed'
